knowledge_fragments.content: Neurological involvement occurs in 5–10% of patients in BD. It is an important manifestation of BD because of its severe morbidity and increased mortality. It usually appears within 5 years after the onset of the disease and is more frequent in men. Central nervous system is more frequently involved than the peripheral nervous system. There are two types of neurological involvement: parenchymal and Nonparenchymal.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 62-year-old male from central Sweden reported experiencing general muscular weakness, weight loss, and increased sweating. The patient had a history of smoking for fifteen years but had quit ten years prior. His medical history included asthma, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and surgically treated bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome. Initial evaluations showed no evidence of malignancy or infection but revealed significantly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). He was administered prednisolone at an initial dose of 40 mg daily, which was later reduced to 20 mg daily, resulting in a decrease in inflammatory markers. One month later, he returned with symptoms of cough and dyspnea on slight exertion. Upon referral to specialized care, he exhibited white sputum, Raynaud’s phenomenon, muscle weakness, and vision loss in the right eye. Examination of his legs and feet revealed red-purple erythema. He also reported pain in both feet and a dorsal extension deficit of the left foot. Neurological evaluation showed no signs of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis was unremarkable.. Confirmed diagnosis: Morbus Adaman

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A previously healthy 9-year-old boy arrived at the emergency department with vomiting and diarrhea following 4 days of fever and 10 days after receiving his second mRNA-SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. He had been exposed to COVID-19 from a family cluster in the previous month, but npRT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 was negative. His family history includes autoimmunity, with his mother having lupus nephritis. Upon arrival, he was conscious but agitated and had low blood pressure (85/45 mmHg). He exhibited fever, conjunctivitis, a rash on his palms, abdominal pain, and headache. On admission, npRT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 was negative, but tests showed positive results for nucleocapsid and spike protein IgG.. Confirmed diagnosis: Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome with neurological involvement. Differential diagnosis includes: Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome with neurological involvement.

knowledge_fragments.content: Neurological involvement occurs in 5–10% of patients in BD. It is an important manifestation of BD because of its severe morbidity and increased mortality. It usually appears within 5 years after the onset of the disease and is more frequent in men. Central nervous system is more frequently involved than the peripheral nervous system. There are two types of neurological involvement: parenchymal and Nonparenchymal.

knowledge_fragments.content: The diagnostic criteria of stroke were formulated according to the “2016 China Stroke Diagnosis and Treatment Consensus.” Diagnostic points are as follows: ① acute onset; ② focal neurological deficit (such as weakness or numbness of one side of face or limb, language disorder); a few patients have comprehensive neurological deficit, which may be accompanied by headache, vomiting, elevated blood pressure, and different degrees of consciousness disorder; ③ symptoms or signs of unlimited duration (when imaging shows responsible lesions) or lasting more than 24 h (when imaging shows no responsible lesions); ④ stroke diagnosed by CT or MRI of the head, with non-cerebral vascular causes excluded.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 62-year-old male from central Sweden reported experiencing general muscular weakness, weight loss, and increased sweating. The patient had a history of smoking for fifteen years but had quit ten years prior. His medical history included asthma, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and surgically treated bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome. Initial evaluations showed no evidence of malignancy or infection but revealed significantly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). He was administered prednisolone at an initial dose of 40 mg daily, which was later reduced to 20 mg daily, resulting in a decrease in inflammatory markers. One month later, he returned with symptoms of cough and dyspnea on slight exertion. Upon referral to specialized care, he exhibited white sputum, Raynaud’s phenomenon, muscle weakness, and vision loss in the right eye. Examination of his legs and feet revealed red-purple erythema. He also reported pain in both feet and a dorsal extension deficit of the left foot. Neurological evaluation showed no signs of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis was unremarkable.. Confirmed diagnosis: Morbus Adaman
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Morbus Adamantiades–Behçet with neurological involvement

tree.case_summary:
A 55-year-old male bodybuilder presents to the emergency department with weakness of his right arm. The patient states he has experienced these symptoms for a few weeks; however, today his hand felt so weak he dropped his cup of tea. The patient has a medical history of diabetes. He drinks 2-7 alcoholic drinks per day and has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. The patient uses anabolic steroids. He has lost 17 pounds since he last came to the emergency department 1 month ago. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 177/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals decreased sensation in the right arm and 2/5 strength in the right arm and 5/5 strength in in the left arm. The patient states that he is experiencing a dull aching and burning pain in his right arm during the exam. Symptoms are not changed with changes in head and neck position. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Apical lung tumor
B. Brachial plexopathy
C. Cerebral infarction
D. Scalenus anticus syndrome
E. Subclavian steal syndrome
